## Claim being audited

The coverage packet shows real progress: `MainProp`, `NashWilliams`, `SuperNW`, `GBetterRelIff`, `Subarr`, `BqoIffGeneralShift`, and `RadoEmbedding` now cover seven configured targets. The six dismissed restriction/Rado tasks have been overtaken and should stay dismissed. The only uncovered targets are `cor PowerQPresBqo`, `thm BqoHerCtblWqo`, and `thm BqoHerCtblWellF`; no hierarchy or hereditary-countability node is present yet. The three open tasks from the prior plan remain mathematically relevant, but they need finer dependency boundaries and one new prerequisite.

The prerequisite is a genuine statement-level blocker. The current declarations `MultiSequence`, `LocallyConstant`, `BadMultiSequence`, and `Bqo` quantify their carrier as `Type`, hence universe 0. A faithful PSet-style hierarchy with atoms in `Q : Type u` and arbitrary nonempty `Type u`-indexed nodes lives in `Type (u+1)`. The probe `.trellis/stuck-math-audit/cycle-10-request-63/universe_obstruction.lean` confirms that even for `Q : Type`, the resulting hierarchy relation cannot instantiate the current `Bqo`. The worker must universe-generalize the reused bqo and super-sequence interfaces in place before introducing the hierarchy; a parallel `LargeBqo` would disconnect the target from the existing DAG.

Paper lines 1362-1426 force a tagged well-founded hierarchy, not `Set Q` and not the existing first-level `SetDomination`. Its lifted relation must expose all four clauses: atom/atom is `r`; atom/node is existential on the right; node/atom is universal on the left; node/node is universal-existential. If raw well-founded tree presentations are used, atom and node tags must remain disjoint, and a structural extensional equivalence plus support/relation invariance must be proved before a target node treats the codes as `PowerQ`. Mutual relatedness under `PowerRel Eq` is not an acceptable presentation equality because it equates an atom with a singleton node.

The preservation proof must follow paper lines 1533-1550. Negation of the four-clause relation supplies Player I's choices, but those choices must be canonical functions of the compared hierarchy values. Arbitrarily choosing a strategy separately for every infinite set would not justify local constancy of the reflected map. The finite-game package therefore needs both termination and a finite-dependence theorem for the copied play along the shift orbit. With that in place, the first target attaches directly to the existing `Bqo`, `MultiSequence`, `LocallyConstant`, `BadMultiSequence`, and `ShiftMap` nodes:

```text
PowerQPresBqo: [IsPreorder Q r] -> Bqo r -> Bqo (PowerRel r).
```

For the hereditary targets, define the carrier literally as the induced part of the full hierarchy that has a countable presentation, rather than replacing the full hierarchy by countably branching trees globally. A robust code is a countably branching tagged tree with `Nat`-indexed node children, erased into the full hierarchy; `HereditarilyCountable x` says that `x` is structurally extensionally equal to such an erasure. This handles finite nonempty nodes by repetition and makes closure under arbitrary nonempty countable families provable.

Paper lines 1559-1581 require a second orientation correction. The present Lean signature of `FrontTreeWellFounded` relates a parent to its proper extension, while well-founded recursion defining `TildeF(s)` from values at strict extensions needs the relation `child parent` iff `parent` is a proper initial segment of `child`. The lane packet already marks the current node's correspondence as failed. Do not use that signature for `TildeF`; add an extension-oriented well-founded helper on the prefix-tree subtype. The resulting `ConverseGame` attaches to `Front`, `PrefixTree`, `ProperInitialSegment`, `SuperSequence`, `BadSuperSequence`, the hereditary node-closure lemma, and `PowerRel`.

The final statements should have the following mathematical shape, with `HerCtblRel r` the restriction of `PowerRel r` to the hereditary carrier:

```text
BqoHerCtblWqo:   [IsPreorder Q r] -> (Bqo r <-> WellQuasiOrdered (HerCtblRel r)).
BqoHerCtblWellF: [IsPreorder Q r] ->
  (Bqo r <-> WellFounded (fun a b => HerCtblRel r a b /\ not HerCtblRel r b a)).
```

For the wqo forward direction, use `PowerQPresBqo`, the elementary implication bqo implies wqo, and restriction to the hereditary subtype. For the reverse direction, turn a bad locally constant multi-sequence into its deciding-front bad super-sequence and apply `ConverseGame`. For the well-founded theorem, wqo implies well-foundedness of the strict part by the Mathlib theorem already imported. The converse must use tail nodes of a bad hereditary sequence: the `(n+1)`-tail is below the `n`-tail, while the badness witness at position `n` prevents the reverse relation. This is the paper's countable-subset argument and avoids the false general assertion that well-foundedness alone implies wqo.

Work in the order listed below. The hereditary core may share definitions with the hierarchy package, but target coverage should be claimed in the order `PowerQPresBqo`, then `BqoHerCtblWqo`, then `BqoHerCtblWellF`. Existing correspondence/substantiveness debts on unrelated covered nodes remain verifier work; they are not reasons to reopen the completed restriction or Rado construction tasks.

superseded_audit_plan.report:
## Claim being audited

The cycle-5 audit prescription to define sub-multi-sequences by `RightComp z` is wrong and must be overturned. It conflates two distinct composition actions which the paper keeps separate. Paper lines 1697-1700 say that the subsets of the fixed set enumerated by `z` are enumerated by `z composed with x`, with `z` fixed on the left and `x` varying on the right. Paper lines 1704-1706 say that shift is instead right composition of the varying enumeration by successor. In the current Tablet convention, `IncSeqComp f g` is `f composed with g`, while `RightComp g f` is `f composed with g`. Consequently the required equations are

```text
ShiftMap x                    = RightComp SuccSeq x = x composed with SuccSeq
correct restriction h z x    = h (IncSeqComp z x)  = h (z composed with x)
current MultiSequenceRestrict = h (RightComp z x)   = h (x composed with z).
```

The compiled probe `.trellis/stuck-math-audit/cycle-6-request-41/composition_orientation.lean` distinguishes the two on noncommuting embeddings. For `z(n)=2*n` and `x(n)=n+1`, `(RightComp z x)(0)=1`, whereas `(IncSeqComp z x)(0)=2`. It also verifies the exact corrected commutation law

```text
IncSeqComp z (ShiftMap x) = ShiftMap (IncSeqComp z x).
```

This orientation is forced semantically: the range of `z composed with x` is contained in the fixed range of `z`; the range of `x composed with z` is instead contained in the varying range of `x` and does not describe a fixed subbase. The earlier probe only checked that `ShiftMap x = x composed with successor`; it did not justify reusing `RightComp z` for subbase restriction.

There is also a direct counterexample to the present `ShiftDichotomy`. Take equality on `{0,1}` and the locally constant map `h(x)=parity(x(0))`. Under the current definition, `(h|z)(x)=parity(x(z(0)))` and `(h|z)(ShiftMap x)=parity(x(z(0)+1))`. For every `z`, the identity embedding makes these parities different, while `x(n)=2*n` makes them equal. Thus no current right-composition restriction is either perfect or bad. This confirms that the problem is mathematical, not merely terminology.

## Structural verdict

The front and shift foundations do not need reconstruction. Keep `IncSeqComp`, `RightComp`, `SuccSeq`, `ShiftMap`, the generalized-shift package, `Front`, `FrontRestrict`, `FrontRestriction`, `SuperSequence`, `SuperSequenceExtension`, `SuperSequenceRestrict`, `FiniteShift`, the deciding-prefix/front/value nodes, `NashWilliams`, `BadMultiToSuper`, `PerfectMultiToSuper`, `BadSuperToBase`, `PerfectSuperToBase`, `BadSuperRestrict`, `PerfectSuperRestrict`, and `NoBadPerfectSuper`. `BaseRightComp` is also a valid operation `x composed with z`; it simply must not be described or used as restriction to the subbase enumerated by `z`.

The false cone must be replaced as a unit: `MultiSequenceRestrict`, `BaseRestrict`, `RestrictionShift`, `RestrictionLocallyConstant`, `BadMultiRestrict`, `PerfectMultiRestrict`, `ShiftDichotomy`, `BaseBqoRestriction`, `PerfectSuperToMulti`, `PerfectBaseToSuper`, and `Subarr`. Some of these nodes state true facts about the current right action, but after the root definition is corrected their signatures or proofs change, and retaining the old statements would preserve the conceptual error. Since this is TheoremStating, repair or delete and recreate these nodes in a single restructure burst; no proof-formalization node-retirement request is legal here.

The dependent arbitrary-base interface should be explicit. A paper-faithful package is:

```text
MultiSequenceRestrict h z : MultiSequence E
  with value at x equal to h (IncSeqComp z x).

BaseRestrict (h : BaseMultiSequence X E) (z : BaseIncSeq X) : MultiSequence E
  with value at x equal to h applied to the subtype enumeration z composed with x.
```

The second parameter must be `BaseIncSeq X`, not an arbitrary `IncSeq`, and the result is most cleanly a global-coordinate multi-sequence. It represents the literal restriction of `h` to the infinite subbase `range z`. Its shift law is the displayed commutation equation, so local constancy and badness/perfectness transports follow for the right reason. If the worker instead chooses a literal dependent codomain `BaseMultiSequence (range z) E`, it must provide the equivalence with this pullback coordinate form and use it consistently; mixing the two presentations is not acceptable.

`ShiftDichotomy` has a second, independent defect in its natural-language proof. It currently colors the deciding front of `h` by comparing a value with an unspecified finite shift. Paper lines 1624-1625 do not do this. They first define the Boolean locally constant map `c_h(x)` recording whether `r (h x) (h (ShiftMap x))`, then form the deciding front of `c_h`, and apply Nash-Williams to the positive subset of that front. The positive and negative homogeneous cases become perfectness and badness only after enumerating the homogeneous subbase and using the corrected restriction/shift equation. The rebuilt statement package needs this Boolean-color layer explicitly; merely flipping the arguments in `MultiSequenceRestrict` leaves the current proof unsound.

Finally, the Lean statement of `Subarr` must express paper line 1656 on arbitrary infinite bases, not only `MultiSequence Q = IncSeq -> Q`. Its middle clause should quantify `X`, a proof that `X` is infinite, and `h : BaseMultiSequence X Q`, and conclude that some `z : BaseIncSeq X` makes `BaseRestrict h z` perfect. The super-sequence clause already carries infinitude through `Front`. A suitable target shape is `Bqo r` equivalent to the conjunction of this arbitrary-base clause and the arbitrary-front clause. Prove `Bqo ->` the base clause by pulling back along an enumeration of `X` and applying the corrected dichotomy; prove the front clause through `SuperSequenceExtension` and the exact subbase `range z`; prove the reverse direction using a bad global multi-sequence, `BadMultiToSuper`, preservation under subfront restriction, and `NoBadPerfectSuper`.

The remaining coverage plan is unchanged only after `Subarr` passes correspondence, substantiveness, and soundness with this interface. The Rado target still belongs downstream of Nash-Williams; the full iterated-powerset and hereditary targets remain governed by process memories pm-0002 through pm-0004. Do not start those packages while the shared restriction interface is false, because the later bad-map and super-sequence transports depend on it.
